title: The mind as friend
hookLine: the mind can be enemy or friend; the Word makes it a friend

lines: A THIRD WAY: O MY MIND.
cards: Three in the morning, and somebody in your head is talking. The bill you forgot. The thing you said at dinner.
The email you haven't answered. A list of what might go wrong tomorrow, read out loud, twice. It's like a roommate who never sleeps and never runs out of news.
You can argue with it, or try to drown it out. The Gurus try a third way. In the Granth, hymns turn to that restless roommate and speak to it directly, almost tenderly.

teach.b: Man, said like mun, is the mind in the Granth: not only the thinking part, but the restless inner self that wants, fears, wanders and chooses. In year one you met it running off in the middle of a prayer.
The Granth is honest that the man can chase everything shiny and drag a person with it.

teach.h: WIN THE MIND, WIN THE WORLD.
teach.b: In the Japji, Guru Nanak puts it in four words, man jeetai jag jeet: win the mind, and you win the world. Some readers hear jeet as conquer; some as win over, the way you'd win over a skeptical friend.
Either way, the struggle is real, and it's inside. Then the mind spoken to as a friend. In Raag Asa, Guru Amar Das addresses it with something close to respect.

teach.h: O MIND, YOU ARE THE FORM OF LIGHT.
teach.b: In paraphrase: O my mind, you are the form of the light; recognize your own source. He doesn't call it garbage. He reminds it who it is.
What turns an enemy into a friend? In the Granth, the answer keeps coming back to the shabad, the Guru's Word.

teach.h: GIVE THE MIND THE WORD TO HOLD.
teach.b: A mind with nothing to hold grabs at everything. A mind given the Word has somewhere to rest. A bored dog chews the furniture, and lies down calm once it has a job.
The Gurus don't throw the mind out of the house. They give it work. So the line between enemy and friend isn't about having a noisy mind.
It's about what the mind is given to hold.

how: Hymns in the Guru Granth Sahib speak directly to the mind, 'O my mind', and Sikhs use the Guru's Word and repetition of the Name, such as Waheguru, to steady it.

o: a person's outer body, as opposed to the soul
the mind: the restless inner self that wants and wanders
the brain alone, the part that does arithmetic

games.q: the mind in the Granth: tap the pairs.
p: win the mind, win the world
O mind, you are the form of light
what the mind is given to hold

s: in the Granth, man means only the thinking brain
it's the whole restless inner self that wants, fears, wanders and chooses.
Guru Amar Das tells the mind it is the form of light
he reminds it to recognize its own source.
the Gurus teach that the mind should be thrown away
they speak to it as a friend and give it the Word to hold.

games.q: it's 3 a.m. and your mind is racing. by today's lesson, which way do you try?
o: argue with every thought until it gives up.
speak to the mind and give it the Word or the breath to hold.
turn on something loud to drown it out.
games.why: the Gurus address the mind, O my mind, and give it the shabad to rest on.

practice: Let the mind do whatever it's doing, and greet each thought the way you'd greet a friend at the door: oh, it's you. Then hand it one thing to hold, Waheguru said softly on the breath if you pray, or the breath itself if you don't.
When it wanders, and it will, don't scold it; just say, O my mind, come back.

wordCard.voice: Man. The mind: the restless inner self that can pull a person away or walk beside them, and that the Guru addresses as the form of light. Today's word.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: man, the mind, the restless inner self.

carryVoice: Your line: befriend the mind. The restless roommate can become a friend. See you tomorrow.
